mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions 'the difference between the number of X and Y', interpret it as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order as given, rather than as an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase 'difference between the number of X and Y' appears, especially in equations equating differences.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between A and B' as |A - B| (absolute value) instead of A - B.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form 'A has N more than B' (including combined forms) into the equation A = B + N, allowing N to be zero or negative if context permits.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a 'has N more than' phrase.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 5 more than B' as A = B - 5 (reversing the sign).

mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement 'X gives N to Y' appears, immediately subtract N from X and add N to Y before processing any later statements.
mathgap.example: Delaying the subtraction from X and addition to Y until after later relational statements, causing those statements to use X's pre‑transfer count.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement 'A has N items' is read, set A's count to N at that moment, allowing later transfers to modify it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: On encountering a direct count statement.
mathgap.example: Treating a direct count as immutable and ignoring later transfers that should change the count.

mathgap.title: Temporal Evaluation of Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: When evaluating a relational statement (e.g., a difference equality), use the current counts of the persons at that point in the sequence, after all prior transfers and assignments have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: On encountering any relational statement that equates differences or compares counts.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count in a relational statement that appears after a transfer affecting that person.

mathgap.title: Combined Sum Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement gives a combined total for several persons (e.g., 'A and B together have N items'), interpret it as the sum of those persons' counts equals N.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A and B together have N' as A = N and B = N separately.

mathgap.title: Split Equally Among Recipients (Additive)
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the donor's count to 0 and add the appropriate share (total divided by number of recipients) to each recipient.
mathgap.example: Splitting a donor's items among recipients but forgetting to set the donor's count to zero.

mathgap.title: Difference Cancellation
mathgap.principle: If an equation equates two differences that share a common term (e.g., X - Y = X - Z), cancel the common term to simplify to Y = Z.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When simplifying difference equations with a shared variable on both sides.
mathgap.example: Cancelling a common term incorrectly when it appears on opposite sides, e.g., treating X - Y = Z - Y as X = Z.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates a difference to another difference (e.g., 'the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of C and D'), translate it into the linear equation (A - B) = (C - D).
mathgap.when_to_apply: On encountering a full difference‑equality statement.
mathgap.example: Treating 'A - B = C - D' as two separate equations A = C and B = D, ignoring the subtraction.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the given order: apply each transfer immediately, then evaluate any relational statements that follow using the updated counts; never evaluate a relational statement with counts that have not yet been updated by preceding transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational statement appears after one or more transfer statements that affect any of the persons mentioned in the relational statement.
mathgap.example: Evaluating 'A - B = C - D' using C's pre‑transfer value even though a transfer to C occurred earlier in the text.

mathgap.description: Treating 'difference between the number of X and Y' as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to interpreting 'difference' as magnitude, ignoring the order of terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two names and treat the expression as X - Y.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model batches updates and applies transfers only at the end, breaking temporal dependencies.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it is read, before any later relational statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming 'A has N more than B' forces A > B and discarding solutions where A - B is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'more' as a strict positivity constraint.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow the equation A = B + N to hold even if N is zero or negative; do not impose extra inequality constraints.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats the assignment as immutable, ignoring subsequent transfer updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as the current value at that point; later transfers may modify it.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model splits an equation like A - B = C - D into A = C and B = D, losing the relational structure.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate the whole equality into a single linear equation (A - B) = (C - D) and solve accordingly.
